objective: Repair the shared CPVS VizieR table parser after a source-backed membership audit failed on a dashed separator row, without changing the CPVS selector or scientific baseline.

previous_knowledge_consumed.detail: A fresh archived-photometry derivation returned 741786 candidates against the 730184 published reference count; the independent membership audit then failed because a dashed separator row was treated as a ZTF name.
Both membership audit paths share read_vizier(); the parser accepted same-width dashed separator rows as data.

change.rationale: Reject only rows whose non-empty fields consist entirely of hyphens, and add regression coverage for the exact separator-row failure. Keep all valid table rows and the name-to-Seq crosswalk unchanged.

expected_improvement: Prevent VizieR separator lines from entering the published membership set.
Allow the shared crosswalk parser to process Table 4 and the selection diagnostic consistently.
Add deterministic regression coverage for the separator-row failure.
Preserve the published reference, SNR thresholds, selector, and v0.2.0 baseline.

correctness.before: A same-width dashed VizieR separator row was parsed as a published ZTF name and caused a false crosswalk failure.
correctness.after: The shared parser skips rows whose non-empty fields contain only hyphens.

reproducibility.before: The retained 100/1000-object samples had not been independently regenerated during this follow-up.
reproducibility.after: Both samples were reproduced exactly from the retained parent/reference/candidate strata using the fixed SHA-256 seed.

validation.evidence: Parser repair and regression tests are committed to the investigation branch. Ordinary CI and the retained-artifact crosswalk have not yet been verified on this head.

root_causes: read_vizier() accepted a VizieR separator row when its tab-delimited field count matched the header; the Table 4 ZTF value then became a dashed string and failed the Table 2 name-to-Seq crosswalk.

findings: VizieR metadata tables can contain dashed separator rows that must be excluded from membership parsing.
A parser-level fix must preserve strict schema, row-count, uniqueness, and crosswalk validation; it must not silently accept malformed object identifiers.

open_blockers: Run the two new separator-row regression tests.
Run the retained-artifact Table 4/Zenodo crosswalk after the tests pass.
A fresh multi-gigabyte source-backed derivation is not yet required; it remains a separate research run.

knowledge_carried_forward: The 741786 versus 730184 membership discrepancy remains unresolved.
Do not add the four-field predicate or tune SNR thresholds to force equality.
Do not repeat multi-gigabyte CPVS acquisition until the bounded parser and crosswalk tests pass.
Seq 615170 has Ng=132 and no rows in the inspected g/r archives; unknown g-archive Seq 615172 has 132 rows. This is an unverified identifier-mapping lead that requires raw coordinate/time comparison.

The fixed 100/1000-object stratified samples from artifact 13108147605 were independently regenerated exactly using seed ztf-cpvs-fixed-object-sample-v2; the design oversamples discrepancy strata and is not a prevalence estimator.
Against the published membership reference, the object-level comparison is TP=730184, FP=11602, FN=0, TN=39816; these are reference-membership metrics, not astrophysical ground-truth performance.
